page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-4GB is a virtualized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to physical AMD EPYC 7542 processors clocked at 2.0 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, providing 4.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate entry-level performance characteristics. The shared CPU allocation limits compute throughput, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core scores falling into the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory performance is similarly constrained; while cached small-block read bandwidth reaches 202.29 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidth drop to 12.62 GB/sec and 10.18 GB/sec, respectively. Geekbench testing yields an average single-core score of 1168.0, but the multi-core score of 2039.0 is weak. For specialized tasks, single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs at an average level of 8.99 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded decompression and software compilation with clang show poor throughput.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this instance represents a budget-friendly tier designed for resource-light workloads rather than intensive production environments. The hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for hosting lightweight applications, development environments, or basic static web serving, which registers a throughput of 2.15 GB/sec. It is also suitable for low-demand background tasks, basic text processing, and small-scale Redis deployments, where it achieves 2.65 million SET operations per second. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
